rows.headline: Indian bonds suffer longest losing streak in three decades due to crude prices and US yields
rows.hook: Thirty-year low for Indian sovereign bonds
rows.summary: Indian government bonds are enduring their worst losing streak in 30 years, driven by persistently high crude oil prices and elevated US Treasury yields. Higher oil prices threaten India's inflation trajectory and fiscal deficit, while rising US yields trigger foreign capital outflows from domestic debt. This macro pressure increases borrowing costs for the government and broader economy, directly impacting fixed-income returns for retail investors.
rows.whats_next: RBI monetary policy committee meeting
rows.why_it_matters: Higher borrowing costs and pressure on fixed-income returns
rows.winners_losers: Borrowers hurt / lenders cautious

rows.headline: Sensex drops 1,575 points and smallcaps crash 7% as Brent hits $114 and rupee nears 95
rows.hook: Record losses hit Indian equities hard
rows.summary: Surging oil prices at $114 per barrel and a weakening rupee near 95 against the dollar wiped out ₹16.1 lakh crore in investor wealth. The Sensex plummeted by 1,575 points, while smallcap stocks suffered a severe 7% crash. This broad market sell-off reflects mounting macroeconomic pressures from rising import bills and currency depreciation. Indian retail investors face heightened volatility and potential erosion of portfolio values across mid and small-cap segments.

rows.why_it_matters: Portfolio values drop sharply as macro headwinds hit Indian equities.

rows.headline: Centre mulls reducing stake in four PSU banks and privatising two lenders
rows.hook: Plans to privatise two public sector banks
rows.summary: The central government is considering reducing its stakes in four public sector banks to 75% to comply with public shareholding norms. Alongside this, plans are underway to privatize at least two public sector lenders in addition to IDBI Bank. This move falls under ongoing efforts to meet minimum public float requirements and reshape state-owned banking. For Indian retail investors, changes in PSU bank ownership could impact valuations and public sector banking index dynamics.
